title: Writable stores with derived state
summary: Share cart state through a store, derive the item count, and read browser storage safely.

scenario.briefing: The cart page crashes during the production build where localStorage does not exist. Rebuild cart.ts so the store hydrates only in the browser, derives the item count, and updates immutably.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Review an artifact and identify the concrete risks.

hints: Guard localStorage with typeof localStorage === "undefined" before reading it.
Export itemCount with derived(cart, function count(lines) and total line.quantity.
Update with [...lines, line] instead of lines.push(line).

misconceptions.description: Calling cart.update and mutating the array in place.
misconceptions.feedback: Svelte compares the value returned by update. A mutated array keeps the same reference, so subscribers may not see a change. Return a new array.
misconceptions.testDescription: Adding a line keeps the existing array.

misconceptions.feedback: The module also runs during a server or prerender build where localStorage is absent. Read browser storage inside a guarded function.
misconceptions.testDescription: The store reads browser storage defensively.

misconceptions.description: Calling subscribe in onMount without returning the unsubscribe function.
misconceptions.feedback: onMount treats a returned function as cleanup. Return the unsubscribe function so the callback stops when the component is destroyed.

sections.title: Stores hold shared reactive state
sections.body: writable creates a store with set and update methods. Any component can subscribe, and the compiler turns a $cart reference into an automatic subscription that is cleaned up with the component.

sections.title: Derived stores compute from their sources
sections.body: derived subscribes to the source stores and recomputes when they change. itemCount stays a read-only projection of the cart instead of a second copy that can drift.

sections.title: Manual subscriptions need cleanup
sections.body: A direct store.subscribe call returns an unsubscribe function. It must be called when the component is destroyed, or the callback keeps running against stale state.

sections.title: Browser APIs are conditional
sections.body: localStorage does not exist during a server or prerender build. Read it inside a guard such as typeof localStorage === "undefined", and treat persisted JSON as untrusted input.

sections.title: The production build changes the assumptions
sections.body: A Svelte build prerenders or server-renders when configured, so module-level browser access runs where window and localStorage are absent. Keep browser access inside functions that run in the browser.

findings.label: The onMount subscription never returns an unsubscribe function.
clearCart mutates the array through $cart instead of calling set or update.
The $cart reference in clearCart leaves a dangling subscription.
The keyed each block causes the subscription to leak.

verdicts.label: Block the change until the subscription has cleanup and the store is updated through set or update.
Ship it; the component is destroyed only when the page closes.

steps.explanation: The manual subscription in onMount runs after the component is destroyed because nothing returns the unsubscribe function. clearCart mutates the array held by the store, so the store never notifies subscribers and derived values go stale. Use $cart in markup or return the unsubscribe function, and replace the array through update.
hints: Check the return value of the onMount subscription.
Check whether clearCart writes through set or update.
Reject findings about automatic $ subscriptions leaking.
Block the change for cleanup and immutability problems.
